STUDY 001 / SHORT-FORM VIDEO

David Mansilla:
Visual Hooks.

131 Reel openings, studied frame by frame. A focused reference library for editors who want to see how the words and visuals work together.

131Reel openings
5Body breakdowns
ENLanguage

WHAT YOU WILL FIND

The edit, made easier to inspect.

01

Opening frames + spoken hooks

Timestamped frames from the first three seconds sit beside the spoken hook and its duration. Original Reel links let you return to the video for context.

02

Three scene-cut groups

82 openings with no cut, 33 with one cut and 16 with two or more cuts. Each group is ordered by observed views, with overall ranks across the 131 Reels.

03

Visual and text classifications

Labels cover the dominant opening element, on-screen text and message category. These are descriptive research labels, not performance scores.

04

Five body breakdowns

Study how selected videos move beyond the opening: script progression, visual changes, pacing, payoff and CTA placement. Drop-off risks are editorial estimates.

RESEARCH NOTES

What the numbers can tell you.

This collection covers one creator and one set of 131 Reels. View counts are a snapshot recorded in the source study, not a live feed or a controlled test. Video age, subject and audience can affect those counts.

The three-second visual window may end before the spoken hook finishes. Hard cuts are counted separately from zooms and overlays. Automated scene detection and transcript tools can introduce errors; source video links provide context.

Message categories in the source may also use caption text, so they should not be read as a pure classification of the spoken opening. Retention graphs are not available to this study. No claim is made that one cut count, visual style or script caused higher views.
